executiveSummary:
Momentum remains strong with ARR growth well above benchmarks and improving operating leverage. Acquisition efficiency is healthy (CAC ratio 0.56; LTV:CAC 6.5), deal flow is consistent, and EBITDA has inflected positively in later periods. The principal constraints are sub-benchmark retention (gross 79%, logo 85%, rolling 12‑month NRR ~92%) and margin performance versus budget (gross margin under, G&A overspend). Expansion is positive but under budget, indicating more of the growth is coming from new logo lands.

  • Stabilise retention and lift NRR: Prioritise diagnosis of churn/downsells via cohort analysis, segment health reviews, and value-realisation checks; consider packaging, entitlements, and CS motions commonly used to reduce logo and revenue churn.
  • Tighten margin and overhead discipline: Review COGS drivers and delivery/support efficiency to recover gross margin; apply pacing and spend controls in G&A consistent with SaaS best practice as profitability improves.
  • Rebalance growth mix toward expansion: Assess pricing and packaging for upsell pathways, evaluate account expansion playbooks, and calibrate sales capacity between land and expand to sustain growth without eroding CAC efficiency.
page1:
Overall health is solid: ARR £9.4m with 70% growth, strong gross (78%) and recurring (83%) margins, and an attractive Rule of 40 at 63%. Efficiency signals are compelling (CAC 0.56; LTV:CAC 6.5; ARR per head 147k). The main weakness is durability: gross retention at 79%, logo retention at 85%, and NRR at 90% lag typical SaaS benchmarks, indicating churn/downsells pressure despite growth.

Management focus reinforced: Retention improvement remains a top priority given the gap between strong acquisition metrics and sub-benchmark NRR.
page2:
Growth is led by consistent land motion: logos increased from 68 to 168 and ARR expanded from £6.8m to £17.6m across the period. Quarterly growth rates are strong (25–47%). Retention oscillates: logo retention ranges 81–100%, net retention improves to 102% by the latest quarter but has been below 100% at points, highlighting underlying variability. Expansion contributes but is not the primary engine; lands dominate ARR adds.

Management focus reinforced: To diversify the growth mix, emphasis on expansion levers (pricing tiers, packaging, customer success expansion motions) would help reduce reliance on new logos and underpin sustained NRR above 100%.
page3:
Operating leverage is improving. S&M % declines from 45% to 24% and G&A from 26% to 19% while Development remains stable ~28–29%. EBIT turns positive and reaches 8% by period end, with Rule of 40 rising to 51%. CAC remains efficient (0.51–0.88 range; latest ~0.51). Headcount scales from 53 to 106, with most growth in Development. Despite this, gross margin underperforms budget (see Budget page), suggesting cost-of-delivery pressure rather than growth drag.

Management focus reinforced: Margin recovery—target COGS drivers (support intensity, hosting, services mix) and tighten G&A pacing to protect the EBIT inflection.
page4:
ARR is diversified across verticals and regions (largest vertical Energy & Utilities £4.0m; regions broadly balanced). Over the last 12 months, ARR grew from £5.8m to £9.7m (+£3.9m), with lands (£4.3m) the dominant contributor; expansions (£0.7m) were smaller, and losses/downsells totaled £‑1.15m. Rolling 12‑month NRR declined from 108% to ~90% mid‑period and recovered to 92%, still below 100%. Vertical NRR is mixed: strong in Utilities and Life Science (≥101%) but weak in Finance & Services (44%).

Management focus reinforced: Prioritise retention and expansion diagnostics in underperforming segments (e.g., Finance & Services), using cohort/segment analyses to quantify drivers and tailor interventions.
page5:
Recent signals (last three months) are positive on new business: +£720k from new logos across 13 wins, with expansions of £180k offset by £45k downsell. Activity is broad-based—Energy & Utilities leads (+£450k total), Government contributes (+£315k), and regions are balanced (Africa and South America +£180k and +£270k respectively). The pattern reaffirms strength in landing while highlighting modest near-term expansion and isolated downsell.

No new management focus items identified on this page.
page6:
Against budget, performance is ahead on ARR (+11% total; additions +8%; attrition better than plan), while upsell trails (‑6%). Revenue is slightly above plan, but gross margin is below (‑13% annual variance). Overheads are mixed: S&M favorable (12%), Development near plan, and G&A materially above (‑38%). Despite margin pressure, EBITDA is modestly ahead of budget.

Management focus reinforced: Gross margin and G&A require attention—typical actions include delivery cost reviews (hosting, support model, services mix) and G&A spend controls, while addressing upsell shortfall through pricing/packaging and expansion playbooks to align growth with plan.
